# switch

## Expression Switch

Switch di Go lebih bersih dan aman daripada di C/Java. **Tidak ada fallthrough otomatis** — setiap case berhenti setelah dieksekusi (tanpa perlu `break`):

```go
hari := "Senin"

switch hari {
case "Sabtu", "Minggu":
    fmt.Println("Akhir pekan!")
case "Senin":
    fmt.Println("Awal pekan, semangat!")
case "Jumat":
    fmt.Println("Hampir akhir pekan!")
default:
    fmt.Println("Hari biasa")
}
// Output: Awal pekan, semangat!
```

## Multiple Values dalam Satu Case

```go
bulan := 4

switch bulan {
case 3, 4, 5:
    fmt.Println("Musim Semi")
case 6, 7, 8:
    fmt.Println("Musim Panas")
case 9, 10, 11:
    fmt.Println("Musim Gugur")
case 12, 1, 2:
    fmt.Println("Musim Dingin")
}
// Output: Musim Semi
```

## Switch Tanpa Ekspresi (Seperti if-else)

```go
suhu := 38.5

switch {
case suhu >= 40:
    fmt.Println("Demam tinggi!")
case suhu >= 38:
    fmt.Println("Demam")
case suhu >= 37:
    fmt.Println("Sedikit panas")
default:
    fmt.Println("Normal")
}
// Output: Demam
```

## Keyword `fallthrough`

Gunakan `fallthrough` untuk meneruskan eksekusi ke case berikutnya (eksplisit):

```go
x := 1

switch x {
case 1:
    fmt.Println("satu")
    fallthrough  // terus ke case 2
case 2:
    fmt.Println("dua")
    fallthrough  // terus ke case 3
case 3:
    fmt.Println("tiga")
case 4:
    fmt.Println("empat")  // tidak dieksekusi
}
// Output:
// satu
// dua
// tiga
```

**Perhatian:** `fallthrough` tidak memeriksa kondisi case berikutnya!

## Type Switch

Type switch digunakan untuk memeriksa tipe dinamis dari interface:

```go
func describe(i interface{}) string {
    switch v := i.(type) {
    case int:
        return fmt.Sprintf("int: %d", v)
    case string:
        return fmt.Sprintf("string: %q", v)
    case bool:
        return fmt.Sprintf("bool: %t", v)
    case []int:
        return fmt.Sprintf("[]int len=%d", len(v))
    default:
        return fmt.Sprintf("unknown type: %T", v)
    }
}

fmt.Println(describe(42))             // int: 42
fmt.Println(describe("hello"))        // string: "hello"
fmt.Println(describe(true))           // bool: true
fmt.Println(describe([]int{1, 2, 3})) // []int len=3
fmt.Println(describe(3.14))           // unknown type: float64
```

## Switch vs if-else Chain

| Aspek | switch | if-else chain |
|---|---|---|
| Keterbacaan | Lebih bersih untuk banyak kasus | Verbosity lebih |
| Fallthrough | Eksplisit dengan `fallthrough` | Tidak ada |
| Type checking | Type switch | Type assertion berulang |
| Performa | Bisa lebih cepat (jump table) | Linear check |
content_en:
# switch

## Expression Switch

Switch in Go is cleaner and safer than in C/Java. **There is no automatic fallthrough** — each case stops after execution (no `break` needed):

```go
day := "Monday"

switch day {
case "Saturday", "Sunday":
    fmt.Println("Weekend!")
case "Monday":
    fmt.Println("Start of the week, stay motivated!")
case "Friday":
    fmt.Println("Almost the weekend!")
default:
    fmt.Println("Regular day")
}
// Output: Start of the week, stay motivated!
```

## Multiple Values in One Case

```go
month := 4

switch month {
case 3, 4, 5:
    fmt.Println("Spring")
case 6, 7, 8:
    fmt.Println("Summer")
case 9, 10, 11:
    fmt.Println("Autumn")
case 12, 1, 2:
    fmt.Println("Winter")
}
// Output: Spring
```

## Switch Without Expression (Like if-else)

```go
temp := 38.5

switch {
case temp >= 40:
    fmt.Println("High fever!")
case temp >= 38:
    fmt.Println("Fever")
case temp >= 37:
    fmt.Println("Slightly warm")
default:
    fmt.Println("Normal")
}
// Output: Fever
```

## The `fallthrough` Keyword

Use `fallthrough` to explicitly continue execution to the next case:

```go
x := 1

switch x {
case 1:
    fmt.Println("one")
    fallthrough  // continue to case 2
case 2:
    fmt.Println("two")
    fallthrough  // continue to case 3
case 3:
    fmt.Println("three")
case 4:
    fmt.Println("four")  // not executed
}
// Output:
// one
// two
// three
```

**Warning:** `fallthrough` does NOT check the next case's condition!

## Type Switch

A type switch is used to check the dynamic type of an interface value:

```go
func describe(i interface{}) string {
    switch v := i.(type) {
    case int:
        return fmt.Sprintf("int: %d", v)
    case string:
        return fmt.Sprintf("string: %q", v)
    case bool:
        return fmt.Sprintf("bool: %t", v)
    case []int:
        return fmt.Sprintf("[]int len=%d", len(v))
    default:
        return fmt.Sprintf("unknown type: %T", v)
    }
}

fmt.Println(describe(42))             // int: 42
fmt.Println(describe("hello"))        // string: "hello"
fmt.Println(describe(true))           // bool: true
fmt.Println(describe([]int{1, 2, 3})) // []int len=3
fmt.Println(describe(3.14))           // unknown type: float64
```

## switch vs if-else Chain

| Aspect | switch | if-else chain |
|---|---|---|
| Readability | Cleaner for many cases | More verbose |
| Fallthrough | Explicit with `fallthrough` | None |
| Type checking | Type switch | Repeated type assertions |
| Performance | Can be faster (jump table) | Linear check |
